messages:
maya: Heads up: After yesterday's auth rollout, we saw an uptick in requests landing with project=null in the billing dashboard. Looks like some exchanged SA tokens are losing their project attribution. Anyone familiar with the change? :confused:
leo: saw that too. Did we change the attribution precedence anywhere in the last deploy?
tess: attribution logic lives in console + auth-service. Console usually reads "project" from X-Project-ID header first, then token.claims.project, then org default. That ordering was intentional to allow proxies to impersonate.
maya: the exchange path we use for SA minting no longer forwards X-Project-ID after refresh (we strip sensitive headers). So if the token claim is missing or malformed we end up defaulting to org.
samir: I dug in  the exchange flow should include the claim for minted SA tokens, but ephemeral tokens created for refresh flows omit the project claim currently. Looks like the token generator path changed to be minimal to satisfy a cross-org edge-case.
leo: for a quick fix can we prefer token.claims over header for internal routes where tokens come from our exchange? That would restore proj attribution for SA flows without affecting partner-injected headers on public routes.
tess: flipping global precedence is risky for partners. But we can make route-level precedence configurable: auth.attribution.precedence = ["claim","header","fallback"]. Default stays header-first. Internal routes set claim-first.
maya: agreed, route-level toggle + telemetry is the way. We should emit an `auth.attribution_source` tag (values: claim|header|fallback) and `token_category` (user|service|ephemeral) plus token_kid to correlate.
nora: product/UX request: expose `auth.attribution_source` and a short explanation in the request inspector panel. Tooltip text: "We prefer token claims for internal system-issued tokens; external header overrides are honored only on public endpoints."
samir: ops/monitoring: add metrics to track `project_attribution_unassigned_pct`, `auth_attribution_source_breakdown`, and `project_mismatch_alerts`. Also set an alert: if `project_attribution_unassigned_pct` > 0.5% over 10m, page eng-platform.
maya: I'll open a PR that implements route-level precedence and adds the telemetry fields + small debug logs when falling back to default (redacting token). The log should include request_id and kid only.
leo: can we do a 1% sampling in prod for the new telemetry first? We don't want to flood observability until the schema is validated.
samir: yes. Plan: staging -> enable feature flag for internal routes; prod: 1% sample for 24h; if stable, ramp to 100% and flip default precedence for exchange routes.
tess: testing checklist: unit tests for precedence ordering, integration test for exchange flow that ensures X-Project-ID is not required when claim present, and an e2e that verifies console displays `auth.attribution_source`.
maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/499 - includes route precedence config, telemetry fields, unit tests.
deploy-bot: deploy started: auth-attrib-route-toggle -> staging at 2025-06-17T09:30:00Z :rocket:
leo: QA notes: watch `auth.attribution_source=claim` requests and confirm project shows up in billing and console. Also check partner proxies still work on public routes (header override respected).
nora: I'll update the inspector copy and add the small help doc in the console docs page. Non-blocking for rollout.
maya: added a non-sensitive debug log: `auth_attrib=fallback reason=missing_claim request_id=req_... kid=kid_...` - redact the kid if it is longer than 8 chars.
samir: telemetry schema update pushed to tracking: add fields `auth_attribution_source`, `token_category`, `token_kid`. I'll coordinate with analytics to consume them.
tess: coordinated rollout plan in ticket INF-824. We'll do 24h observation post-1% sample, then 10% for 2h, then 100%.
maya: small nit: ensure the exchange path doesn't strip X-Project-ID for internal service-to-service calls where the header is meaningful. We should avoid two possible fixes fighting each other.
leo: agree. Let's make the code tolerant: if X-Project-ID present, but claim present too, log when they disagree and set `project_mismatch=true` for telemetry.
nora: I'll add UI for `project_mismatch` in the request inspector to help debug cases where header vs claim differ.
maya: thanks everyone. I'll watch staging and escalate if `project_attribution_unassigned_pct` spikes.
